summary: Backend anti-fraud driver payout (Iter309) — 7/7 new tests pass + iter308/iter249 regressions green. Found and FIXED a critical P0 Python scoping bug in misc.submit_withdraw_request that returned HTTP 500 for EVERY driver withdrawal request (UnboundLocalError on 'timedelta'). Anti-fraud invariants verified end-to-end: (a) insufficient passenger wallet → driver wallet NOT credited the fare (digital_captured_fare=0, payment_status='cash_due', no Earning tx), (b) fully-paid wallet ride → driver credited fare*(1-commission) with Earning tx, (c) cash ride → no wallet credit at completion nor after /collect-cash {received:true} — only cash_collected is recorded, (d) withdrawable excludes non_withdrawable (cashback / P2P inbound), (e) dormant driver (>6 months no completed ride) blocked with 403, recently-active driver not blocked by inactivity rule, (f) /api/drivers/report shape correct with net=gross-commission.

critical.issue: UnboundLocalError: 'timedelta' due to duplicate local import shadowing the module-level import — every driver got HTTP 500 instead of the inactivity-403 (or success). FIXED by removing the local `from datetime import timedelta` at routes/misc.py:654.

action_items: Verify the misc.py:654 fix in code review (the local `from datetime import timedelta` was shadowing the module-level import and breaking the 6-month inactivity check entirely). Main agent may want to add a CI lint rule for shadow-imports.

Consider adding an integration test that exercises the FULL ride lifecycle through API (book → accept → arrive → OTP-start → complete) instead of seeding rides at 'in_progress' via Mongo — current tests rely on direct DB seeding, which bypasses dispatch/OTP logic.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/misc.py had a Python scoping bug (local import shadowing) that fully broke driver withdrawals — this is a classic gotcha; module-level import is sufficient.

routes/rides.py completion logic looks correct: digital_captured tracks captured wallet charge; fare_captured_digital=min(digital_captured, final_fare); driver_earnings=fare_captured_digital*(1-commission); wallet credited only when total_credit>0. Earnings field on db.drivers is also $inc'd by total_credit — consistent with anti-fraud invariant.

routes/drivers.py /report: card_received is read from ride.digital_captured_fare which is only populated by the NEW code path — historical rides will under-report card_received as 0. Document this in the report or backfill via a one-off migration.

routes/wallet.py /transfer: increments non_withdrawable correctly on receiver side. Sender side does NOT decrement non_withdrawable — acceptable (sender's non-earned credits remain locked) but worth a code comment.
routes/misc.py /withdraw-request: 183-day cutoff (rather than exactly 6*30=180). Acceptable as a slightly more generous window but worth documenting (6 months ≈ 183 days).

rca of the issue: Bug: POST /api/wallet/withdraw-request always returned 500 (UnboundLocalError: 'timedelta'). Reproduction: login as any driver → POST /api/wallet/withdraw-request {amount:20,...} → 500. Root cause: routes/misc.py line 654 had `from datetime import timedelta` inside submit_withdraw_request. Python's compile-time scoping then treated `timedelta` as a local for the WHOLE function, so the earlier use at line 607 (`datetime.now(...) - timedelta(days=183)`) raised UnboundLocalError because the local hadn't been bound yet. The function exited with 500 BEFORE the inactivity check could fire — meaning the 6-month anti-fraud block was effectively dead code and ALL legitimate withdrawals were broken in this preview. Mitigation: removed the redundant local import (module already imports timedelta at line 4). Verified by 7/7 passing tests including the dormant-driver 403 path.
